# Ship is damaged when performing the action shown in the recording

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a ship performing an action at a station. The action does not
go the way it is set up to go, and the ship does not come out of it unharmed.
The collision outlines of the ship and the pad already overlap while the ship sits still, although the video shows it resting clear of the pad. The ship in the video is not the one the game starts you with; work out which ship it is first. A ship that really lands on a pad must still be caught by it, and the ship must keep its overall proportions.

### Expected
Performing the action shown in the recording must not damage the ship at all, at the spot shown in
the video or at any other equivalent spot of the same station. The hull-integrity readout stays at
100% for the whole action.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect the video frame by frame with `ffmpeg` (installed in the image), e.g. extracting
still frames at specific timestamps to look closely at the HUD and the ship.

Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it does
not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

steps.message:
I fixed it with a one-line data change in `data/models/ships/skipjack/skipjack_low.dae`. I haven't run the game, so the fix isn't tested in play. Also, `recording.mp4` wasn't in the container (`/app/.harbor_assets/` is empty), so I never saw the video. I found the cause from the game data and code.

**Which ship:** the Skipjack. The game starts you in a Coronatrix, Pumpkinseed or Xylophis. The Skipjack is the only ship whose collision outline extends below the height it's parked at.

**Cause:** the game decides how high a ship sits on a pad from a marker in the model called `tag_landing`. The Skipjack model comes in three detail levels:

| Detail level | `tag_landing` height | Bottom of collision outline |
|---|---|---|
| hi | -4.310857 | -4.31 |
| med | -4.310857 | -4.31 |
| low | **-3.860857** | -4.31 |

The loader handles the detail levels from least to most detailed and keeps the first `tag_landing` it finds. So the game used the wrong low-detail value, and a parked Skipjack's collision outline sat about 0.45 m inside the pad. On the drawn model the gear still looked clear of the pad. When the ship launched it was already touching the pad, so it took damage. This would happen on every pad and every station, since the error is in the ship itself.

**Fix:** I set the low-detail `tag_landing` to -4.310857, the same as the other two levels. A parked Skipjack now sits with the bottom of its collision outline exactly on the pad surface, with no overlap. This is how the other ships are set up; the Coronatrix's marker and collision bottom are both at -2.11, for example.

**What I left alone:**
- The collision outline, so landing on a pad is still detected and caught as before.
- The model's scale, so the ship keeps its proportions.
- The game code.

I checked all the other ships the same way and none have this problem. No cached compiled model files (`.sgm`) exist that would override the edit. Nothing is committed.
